title: Is Ceramic Coating Worth It? What It Does and Who It Suits
meta_description: Ceramic coating is worth it if you're keeping the car, the paint is corrected first and you wash it gently. What it does, what it won't, and the cheaper options.
excerpt: A ceramic coating is worth it for some cars and a waste on others. What it does and doesn't do, why the preparation matters most, and when a sealant is the better buy.

hero.alt: Glossy black Audi SUV bonnet, headlight and front wing after a wash on a brick driveway

faq.q: Does a ceramic coating stop scratches and stone chips?
faq.a: No. It's a thin layer that makes the paint easier to keep clean, but a brush wash, a dirty sponge or a stone will still mark it. Paint protection film is the product for stone chips.

faq.q: How long does a ceramic coating last?
faq.a: It's the longest-lasting of wax, sealant and coating, but how long depends on the product and how the car is washed. We offer longer-life options and talk you through them when we quote; our Protection Detail's ceramic sealant lasts about 6 months.

faq.q: Is it worth putting a ceramic coating on an older car?
faq.a: It can be, if you're keeping it and the paint is machine polished first. If the paint is swirled and the car isn't being polished, a coating will just protect the swirls.

faq.q: Can I take a ceramic coated car through an automatic car wash?
faq.a: We'd avoid brush washes. The coating won't stop the brushes leaving swirls, and you'll lose the finish you paid for. A careful hand wash with a pre-wash and two buckets keeps it at its best.

faq.q: Is a ceramic sealant the same as a ceramic coating?
faq.a: No. A sealant is a thinner layer that's quicker to apply and doesn't need polishing first; ours lasts about 6 months. A coating lasts longer but needs the paint corrected and dry weather to cure.

cta.heading: Thinking about a ceramic coating?
cta.text: We decontaminate, polish and coat the paint, and tell you honestly if a sealant would suit the car better. Coatings are booked by quote.

Is a ceramic coating worth it? For a car you're keeping for years, with the paint corrected first and washed gently, yes: it's the longest-lasting protection and makes every wash quicker and easier.

But it won't stop stone chips, it isn't scratch-proof, and it seals in whatever is underneath, swirls included. For a lot of daily drivers, a ceramic sealant is the better buy.

Our new guide explains what a coating does and doesn't do, why the preparation matters more than the bottle, and how to tell which option suits your car.
share.instagram:
Is a ceramic coating worth it? Only if the paint underneath is worth locking in.

A coating seals in whatever condition the paint is in. Coat swirled paint and you get well-protected swirls. That's why every coating we do starts with a full decontamination, clay bar and machine polish, and why it's booked around the weather: it needs dry conditions to cure.

Keeping the car for years and washing it gently? It's worth it. Selling soon or using brush washes? A sealant will serve you better.
